diagnosis: The skill has reached a local optimum because it is attempting to serve two conflicting purposes within a single, monolithic document: it is both a step-by-step procedural guide for an AI agent and a comprehensive user manual for a human. Initial mutations improved its quality as a user manual, achieving a perfect score. Subsequent mutations attempted to bolt on an agent-specific execution guide. While this also achieved a perfect score, the skill is now bloated. Any further mutation that improves human readability (e.g., adding more explanatory context) likely degrades agent performance by adding noise, and any change that optimizes for the agent (e.g., removing context) degrades human usability. The system is stuck because it cannot improve one aspect without harming the other, and the current evaluation suite is not sensitive enough to reward a separation of these concerns.

The skill is stuck in a local optimum of "procedural perfection." Past mutations have successfully built an extremely clear, linear, and robust step-by-step guide for an AI agent. The skill now perfectly handles prerequisites, execution, and multiple layers of fallbacks, which is why it consistently scores 36/36 on the existing test suite. The optimization loop is now making micro-refinements to a process that already works flawlessly according to the tests. The root cause of the stagnation is that the skill has become a bloated, monolithic document trying to serve as both a concise agent-facing prompt and an exhaustive human-facing user manual. This dual identity prevents further meaningful improvement; any change to improve one aspect risks confusing the other, and the tests aren't sophisticated enough to reward the next level of improvement: agentic efficiency and conciseness.
